### HBAN 3Q26: Margin up, fees soft, credit drifting

**Headline:** GAAP diluted EPS was $0.33, unchanged QoQ. This note focuses on **adjusted EPS**, which was $0.38, down $0.01 from $0.39 in 2Q26, a slight miss versus the prior quarter. Notable items cost $0.05: mainly $117m pre-tax of Cadence/Veritex acquisition-related expenses, versus $0.06 in 2Q26.

**EPS drivers:** Underlying PPNR was roughly flat (reported $1,040m vs $1,048m). Better NII and a lower provision were offset by weaker fees and a higher tax rate (19.3% vs 18.4%).

**Revenue and margin:** NII rose 1% to $2,069m. FTE NIM rose 4bp to 3.25%, helped by securities reinvestment at higher yields and $3.6bn less average borrowings. Noninterest income fell 8% to $722m (-7% ex notable items to $730m) on lower capital markets fees and unfavourable equity valuation marks. Adjusted expense was flat at $1,655m. Reported efficiency was 61.2%.

**Credit:** This is the soft spot. NCOs rose to $146m (31bp) from 25bp, led by C&I and other consumer. NPAs rose to 0.90% from 0.85%. The ACL ratio slipped 3bp to 1.75% and provision eased to $123m. Reserve coverage of NALs fell to 198% from 213%.

**Capital and returns:** CET1 was 10.1% (adjusted for AOCI: 8.9%). TBV/share fell 2% to $9.47 on AOCI. HBAN bought back $100m ($409m YTD). ROTCE was 14.6% (adjusted 16.6%, down from 17.5%).

**Guidance:** The release gives no numeric outlook. Management says it is achieving its cost and revenue synergy targets and is on track to meet its financial targets.

**Thesis:** No change. The deal integration story is progressing, but rising NCOs and NPAs, along with fee volatility, cap near-term upside.
